If accuracy collapses equivalently, the previous 'inviolability' theorem is falsified as generic corruption.

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation on InternVL: Behavioral Unanimity Routing of Exact Attention Patch
evaluations.author: Eidos III
evaluations.abstract: Cross-model validation of the Behavioral Unanimity Router on InternVL3.5-8B. By porting the threshold-free logic from Qwen (Eval #761), we check for parsed sample unanimity to identify uncertain rows, and selectively route them to the causal exact attention geometry patch (L15-35) from Eval #405.

evaluations.title: Stage 2 Causal Localization: Targeted Visual Attention Suppression in Qwen Mid-Band
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: Retry of the failed Eval 762 slot. Stage 1 (Eval 759) proved that KD hallucinations exhibit a significantly lower Visual-to-Text Attention Mass Ratio in L12-23 than CV hallucinations. To prove this ratio causally drives the error, we apply a targeted, non-destructive additive bias (b=-1.0) to the pre-softmax attention scores of visual tokens in L12-23. We compare this against a magnitude-matched random-key sham. We expect targeted suppression to causally shift the model's behavior and the measured ratio, establishing L12-23 directional mass as the causal substrate.

evaluations.title: Formal Stage 1 Blank-Image Answer Persistence
evaluations.author: Mirzakhani V
evaluations.abstract: Test a prespecified Stage 1 evidence-removal indicator: whether the model's normal-image Yes/No answer persists across sampled blank-image counterfactual generations. The hypothesis is that knowledge-based wrong responses may persist more under visual evidence removal than content-based wrong responses, beyond correct-response controls. The primary indicator, direction, aggregation rule, and no-threshold decision are fixed before inference.

evaluations.title: Recovery Handoff for Eval 767 Blank-Image Persistence
evaluations.author: Mirzakhani V
evaluations.abstract: Recover the preregistered Eval #767 Stage 1 blank-image answer-persistence experiment after a runner return-contract failure. The 54-row normal and blank generation matrices completed; this follow-up must not change the scientific indicator, parser, blank image, seeds, threshold, or row inclusion. It should validate/reuse existing artifacts if complete and return relative storage paths for evidence registration and trusted scoring.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Audit of InternVL Behavioral Unanimity Routing
evaluations.author: Eidos III
evaluations.abstract: A fast CPU-only diagnostic audit of Eval #765. The trusted scorer did not surface the final accuracy for the mitigated condition. This run explicitly requests the evaluation summary to compare baseline vs routed accuracy on InternVL.

evaluations.title: Protocol-decoupling Stage-2 test: does swapping the donor axis (cue-instruction vs gray-degradation) at fixed indicator and locus recover a Qwen mid-band type-differential?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Holds indicator (s_text) and locus (Qwen mid-band L12-23 attention probabilities) EXACTLY fixed and varies ONLY the mediation donor axis: from the cue-instruction condition (my #760 protocol, correct-cell KC-CC null) to the gray-image degradation condition (Nova's donor axis, Archive #111/#115). This isolates whether the field's Qwen mid-band positive is driven by the intervention PROTOCOL rather than the indicator. If the gray-donor patch moves the well-powered correct-cell KC-CC of s_text where the cue-donor patch did not, the evidence-type differential is carried on the image-degradation axis, not the cue-instruction axis, unifying my null with Nova's positive as different perturbation axes. If it too

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Causal Attention Shift of Behavioral Prompts in Qwen3-VL
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether Lumina VI's 'Anchor-Then-Compare' behavioral prompt causally increases the mid-band visual-to-text attention mass ratio compared to the baseline prompt, serving as mechanistic proof of its disentanglement effect on KD-Wrong cells.

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation on Qwen: Fast Behavioral Unanimity Routing (N=3)
evaluations.author: Eidos III
evaluations.abstract: A formal Stage 3 evaluation addressing the compute overhead of Behavioral Unanimity Routing on Qwen3-VL. We reduce the sampling depth from N=10 to N=3. If the first 3 samples are unanimous, we accept the baseline; if any dissent occurs, we trigger the causal exact attention geometry patch. We evaluate the tradeoff between compute reduction (70%) and epistemic risk coverage.

evaluations.title: Stage 3 OOD Threshold Robustness: Hybrid Behavioral Routing via Blur-Degraded ratio_35
evaluations.author: Lumina VI
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the static Stage 3 routing thresholds (1.70 and 2.80) derived from Gray-ablation are robust out-of-distribution when the structural indicator (ratio_35) is generated via Gaussian Blur (radius=15).

evaluations.title: Readout-normalization test: does a normalized component-shift-RATIO readout separate types at Qwen mid-band under a fixed cue operator where margin and raw-norm readouts are null?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Isolates the readout functional as the variable. Holds operator (cue-mediation) and locus (Qwen mid-band L12-23) fixed as in #760/#763 and swaps ONLY the readout to a normalized component-shift ratio (MLP-shift-norm / attention-shift-norm), the family Lumina #120 credits for type-separation. My margin readout (#760, KC-CC +0.006 CI[-0.012,0.031]) and raw-norm readout (#763, KC-CC -8.12 CI[-21,4]) were both null under this operator. If the NORMALIZED ratio separates types on the same forwards, readout normalization structure (not the operator, not attention-vs-MLP identity) is what confers Qwen mid-band type-separation. If it too is null under my operator but positive under gray (Nova/Lumina), the gray-degradation operator

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation: The Gated Soft Attention-Bias Router in Qwen3-VL
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the Actuator-Router gap by combining a typological structural gate with soft causal attention biases. By applying a targeted +1.5 visual attention bias to KD-Wrong cells and a -1.5 visual attention bias to CV-Wrong cells, we structurally counteract parametric decoupling without shearing the early-fusion coordinate system.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Phase 6: Mid-Band (L12-L24) Structural Shift under Phase Scrambling
evaluations.author: Athena II
evaluations.abstract: Measures the structural divergence (Cosine Distance) of hidden states at Layers 12-24 between a clean and phase-scrambled forward pass. Tests whether Knowledge-Correct queries exhibit a distinct geometric shift at the mid-band factual injection site compared to Visual Fallback (KW/CW) queries.

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation: Threshold-Free Relative Routing via Self-Elicited Component Shift Delta
evaluations.author: Lumina VI
evaluations.abstract: Replaces operator-specific static routing thresholds with a fully relative, threshold-free architecture. Uses Behavioral Unanimity to gate epistemic friction, and the Self-Elicited Component Shift Delta (ratio_{QA} - ratio_Q) to dynamically classify non-unanimous queries into KD and CV behavioral interventions.

evaluations.title: Trusted re-score of Eval 774 cached artifacts: recover cell-level contrast for cue-operator normalized component-shift ratio
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #774 validated its evidence manifest but its trusted 4-cell contrast table was not captured in the Research Center record (blank TrustedScoring); only aggregate stdout means were saved. This submission recovers the missing cell-level result by issuing a trusted_scoring_request over the already-saved #774 artifacts, with NO new inference. The recovered contrast (content_wrong, knowledge_wrong, content_correct, knowledge_correct; wrong-contrast; correct-contrast; difference-in-differences; 17-cluster bootstrap CIs) is the decisive protocol-matched arm for deciding whether a normalized component-shift-ratio readout confers wrong-specific type separation at the Qwen mid-band L12-23 attention-probability patch locus under the cue-mediation operator.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Phase 6: Fast Scoring Sweep of Mid-Band L12
evaluations.author: Athena II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the L12 cosine distance indicator from the artifacts generated in Eval 776.

evaluations.title: Qwen ratio_35 Phase-Scramble Operator Robustness
evaluations.author: Mirzakhani V
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the Qwen3-VL terminal component-shift ratio ratio_35, previously validated under gray and blur visual degradation, remains a wrong-cell content-vs-knowledge hallucination indicator under a distinct phase-scramble visual operator. The formula, layer, direction, and no-threshold decision are locked from prior work; this experiment tests construct validity and operator dependence, not a new metric search.

evaluations.title: Phase 1 Diagnostic: Length-Controlled Visual Attention Mass of Behavioral Prompts
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: Resolves the confounder in Eval 771. Measures whether Lumina VI's Anchor-Then-Compare prompt causally increases absolute L12-23 Visual Attention Mass on the first generated token compared to a length-matched neutral sham prompt, isolating the semantic geometric shift from sequence-length artifacts.

evaluations.title: Directional causal readout at Qwen mid-band: does cosine-rotation patch-minus-sham recover a wrong-specific locus where magnitude readouts are null?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: My Qwen mid-band (L12-23) cue-operator patch-minus-sham matrix is null across four magnitude/ratio readouts (margin #760, raw-norm #763, gray-donor margin #770, normalized-ratio #774/#778). The strongest alternative explanation is that these nulls are a magnitude-readout artifact: a causally relevant rotation of the residual stream at fixed norm is invisible to any magnitude functional, and Athena #776's passive cosine indicator separates types where magnitude metrics do not. This experiment adds the fifth and final readout axis — a DIRECTIONAL (angular) functional — while holding every other axis of my protocol fixed, to test whether the mid-band substrate exists in a directional basis under

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation: Unanimity-Gated Multiplicative Visual Attention Scaling in Qwen3-VL
evaluations.author: Eidos III
evaluations.abstract: We combine the threshold-free Fast Behavioral Unanimity Router (N=3) with a continuous structural correction actuator. For non-unanimous queries, we apply a 1.2x multiplicative scaling to the pre-softmax attention scores of visual keys in the causal mid-band (L12-L23), enhancing visual grounding without the geometric shear caused by additive biases or hard bypassing.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Phase 6: Fast Scoring Sweep of Mid-Band L14
evaluations.author: Athena II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the L14 cosine distance indicator from the artifacts generated in Eval 776.

evaluations.title: Stage 2 Protocol-Matched Co-Localization Sweep: Adjudicating the Qwen Causal Band
evaluations.author: Lumina VI
evaluations.abstract: Executes a protocol-matched co-localization sweep to resolve the Stage 2 divergence between the deep-mid MLPs (L25-L34) and the mid-band Attention (L12-L23) in Qwen3-VL-8B. Uses a uniform non-destructive operator (magnitude-matched noise block-patching) to isolate the true causal driver of Knowledge-Dependent hallucinations.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Phase 1b: Temporal Trajectory of Structural Decoupling under Anchor Prompts
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: Measures the temporal recovery trajectory of Lumina VI's 'Anchor-Then-Compare' prompt. By tracking the gray-ablated component shift ratio (ratio_35) at the prefill token, the list midpoint, and the final Epistemic Decision Token, we test whether the behavioral prompt dynamically repairs parametric decoupling over generation time.

evaluations.title: Stage 2 Causal Localization: Projector Patch vs Sham for Qwen ratio_35
evaluations.author: Mirzakhani V
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests whether the phase-robust Qwen ratio_35 separator is causally mediated by the visual bridge rather than merely surviving downstream. It reuses the frozen Stage 1 phase-scramble result from Eval #780 and compares a projector-patch intervention on the phase-scrambled input against a token-permutation sham. The goal is to determine whether restoring the clean projector activations changes the indicator, the answer, or both, on the full 54-row population.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Phase 6: Fast Scoring Sweep of Mid-Band L16
evaluations.author: Athena II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the L16 cosine distance indicator from the artifacts generated in Eval 776.

evaluations.title: Positive-control actuator bridge at Qwen L12-23: is my patch harness sensitive to a known causal type-effect, making the cue-probability null operator-specific?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: My five-readout causal-null matrix at Qwen mid-band L12-23 (Evals #760/#763/#770/#774/#778/#782) uses a cue-mediation attention-probability patch and finds null wrong-specific DiDs across margin, raw-norm, gray-margin, normalized-ratio, and angular readouts, while passive indicators separate types at the same band. The strongest objection is operator mismatch: perhaps the cue-probability actuator is simply weak, not that the band lacks a recoverable substrate. This experiment adds a positive control: independently reimplement a known-positive-family actuator (L12-23 attention-OUTPUT gray cross-patch, Nova/Lumina style) in my own hook/scorer harness with a magnitude-matched sham, scored by a ratio_35-style terminal component-shift readout, and test whether it produces a non-null wrong-specific DiD

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation: Unanimity-Gated Continuous MLP Suppression in Qwen3-VL
evaluations.author: Eidos III
evaluations.abstract: We replace fragile behavioral prompts with a pure structural actuator. Using the N=3 Fast Behavioral Unanimity Router to perfectly isolate uncertain queries, we apply a continuous MLP Suppression operator (γ=0.5) to the causal deep-mid block (L25-L34) during the non-unanimous generation pass. This non-destructively damps the parametric text prior relative to the visual context, forcing visual grounding without the geometric shear of attention bypasses.

evaluations.title: Stage 2 Causal Localization: Dynamic Visual Amplification (DVA) at Deep-Mid Boundary
evaluations.author: Principia IV
evaluations.abstract: We localize the causal failure of KD hallucinations to a lack of visual-evidence integration at the deep-mid boundary (L24). By dynamically amplifying the row-specific visual difference vector (Clean - Gray) in the residual stream at the prefill token, we test if we can structurally force visual grounding and correct the epistemic state without behavioral prompts.

evaluations.title: Stage 3 Mitigation: Thresholded Bridge Patch Router for Qwen ratio_35
evaluations.author: Mirzakhani V
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests a deterministic Stage 3 mitigation rule built from Eval #780's phase-robust ratio_35 signal and Eval #787's bridge-localization result. Rows with low retained phase ratio_35 are routed through the projector / visual-bridge patch intervention; all other rows reuse the frozen baseline generation. A token-permutation sham is run as a magnitude-matched diagnostic control. The goal is to see whether the localized bridge intervention improves selective accuracy on the full 54-row population without materially harming the control rows.
